title: The Mitchell Four gospel quartet
summary: Childhood quartet with siblings, learning from the Robinson Humming Four, church programs.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: When I was about, I'd say about six years old, when I was, we had a quartet group, you know. My brothers and I. What you sang?

That's my first encounter with music, you know. Now, I was the youngest in the group, and my brother Ulyss, and my brother Emile, and my sister was a leader, you know. I had another sister younger than me, and another brother, too, and you know, but they wasn't born, you know. Right. Right. And they were, you know, after me, it was almost a baby, and then something. But anyway, we used to, used to have a, some man had a quartet named the Robinson Hummin' Four, you know.
Robinson Hummin' Four, sure. Robinson Hummin' Four. Robinson Hummin' Four.
Go ahead. Oh but then they stood me. No, no, no, no. We'll just move back up a little bit. That's okay. That's fine.

Go ahead. Yeah. So they used to come on Corinth Street between General Logan and Eagle. And the baritone singer, he used to live there. And they used to rehearse there, you know. And so me and my brother used to go sit on the porch and listen at them, you know. And we'd listen, I'd listen at the tenor player, I mean the guy that sang tenor.
Well the singer, the singer. Yeah.

And he'd listen at the baritone part, my other brother listened at the bass part, my sister would listen to the lead. And so they was practicing one time and after they took a little break, well we started singing out there on the porch. We used to be on the porch listening at them inside. And then after a while they heard us singing and they came out there and said, was y'all singing?
He said, yeah. And they made us come in and sing with them, you know.
And so after that we decided so good until they started bringing us on some of their programs, you know. And we got to be very popular singing in those churches.
Now what was your group name? What was your group name? The Mitchell Four.

You called yourself The Mitchell Four. The Mitchell Four. I was about six years old then, you know. And we used to sing, you know, we wouldn't sing for no money or nothing, we just did it because we liked it, you know. But one time we were singing and they had a lady pick up some collection and she gave me the money, you know. I thought she meant for me to put it in the collection basket so I put it in there. And she said, I meant that was for y'all, you know. But anyway, we got to be very popular all up through Colton and one time we went to a church convention and slide there, you know, that's my first time being away from the mall, you know, small kid.

Yeah, slide there. That didn't look like a long way then. Slide out and hammering, you know, we sung all through there for convention. And my dad, well that's the only time I seen him let my mother go that far without him. You know, he had to stay home with my little younger sister. And so we got pretty good, I think if we would have kept on, we might have really made it good,
